 KRA announces deadline for taxpayers seeking 100% waiver on penalties and interest
 Saturday 07th November, 2026 09:47 AM | 
 By Ndiritu Wanjiru 
 Ndiritu Muriithi. PHOTO/https://www.facebook.com/ndiritu.muriithi.3 
 The Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) has reminded taxpayers with outstanding tax liabilities to take advantage of the ongoing Tax Amnesty Programme, warning that the opportunity to secure a 100 per cent waiver on eligible penalties and interest will close on December 31, 2026. 
 In a statement issued on Saturday, November 7, 2026, KRA urged individuals and businesses with pending tax obligations to take advantage of the programme before the deadline to avoid missing out on the relief.
 The authority emphasised that the opportunity was still available, stating that the opportunity to benefit from the ongoing Tax Amnesty Programme was still open.
 “The opportunity to benefit from the ongoing Tax Amnesty Programme is still open! If you have outstanding tax liabilities, you could qualify for 100% forgiveness on eligible penalties and interest under Tax Amnesty 2026. Take advantage of the programme before 31st December 2026,” KRA stated.
 KRA’s statement on tax amnesty. PHOTO/A screengrab by PD Digital posted by @KRACare/X. 
 How taxpayers can benefit from the amnesty 
 Under the Tax Amnesty 2026 programme, eligible taxpayers can receive a full waiver of accumulated penalties and interest on qualifying outstanding tax liabilities.
 This means that taxpayers who owe taxes alongside additional charges arising from penalties and interest could have those extra costs waived if they meet the programme’s requirements.
 However, the relief does not automatically cancel the original tax debt. Taxpayers are still required to settle the principal tax amount in accordance with the applicable amnesty conditions.
 KRA highlighted the benefit in its statement, noting that taxpayers with outstanding liabilities could qualify for 100% forgiveness on eligible penalties and interest under Tax Amnesty 2026.
 What taxpayers should do before December 31 
 With the deadline approaching, taxpayers with outstanding obligations are encouraged to log in to the KRA iTax portal and review their tax records to establish whether they have unpaid taxes, penalties or accumulated interest.
 They should then establish whether their outstanding liabilities qualify for the Tax Amnesty 2026 programme and determine how much of the accumulated penalties and interest could be waived.
 Taxpayers should also review the principal tax amount owed and familiarise themselves with the applicable payment and application requirements. Those who qualify should follow the procedures provided by KRA and ensure they complete the necessary steps within the stipulated period.
 A woman files her tax returns on the KRA website. Image used for illustration 
 Individuals and businesses with questions about their eligibility or the application process can seek clarification through KRA’s official website and customer service channels.
 KRA issues December 31 warning 
 KRA has set December 31, 2026, as the final date for taxpayers seeking to benefit from the programme.
 The authority urged eligible taxpayers to act before the deadline, warning that those who fail to take advantage of the initiative within the stipulated period risk missing the opportunity to have their eligible penalties and interest waived.
 “Take advantage of the programme before 31st December 2026,” KRA stated.
 The reminder gives individuals and businesses that may have accumulated tax debts an opportunity to review their outstanding obligations and address them before the end of the year.
